clue.text: The crowning glory for this lovely lady !

definitions.text: The crowning glory for this lovely lady !

parts.words: The crowning glory for this lovely lady
parts.note: a pageant winner is literally crowned, so her crowning glory is the tiara placed on her head

explanation.surface: A compliment about a pretty woman's hair, usually called her crowning glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowning glory' normally means fine hair; here it is the moment a contest winner is crowned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant winner is the lovely lady who receives a crown as her prize.

clue.text: Stand around reading things!

definitions.text: Stand around reading things!

parts.note: a stand with printed matter all around it, such as a kiosk at a railway station

explanation.surface: Idlers loiter and read whatever is lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand around' suggests loitering, but the stand is a stall surrounded by things to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk selling newspapers and paperbacks is a stall surrounded by reading matter.

clue.text: Attacks Curly-alias " Ship"

definitions.text: Attacks

indicators.note: curly hair is twisted about, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, prefixed to ships' names

explanation.surface: A ship's crewman nicknamed Curly launches assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curly' looks like a nickname but signals rearranging ALIAS together with SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assails and attacks are synonyms, both meaning launches an assault on.

clue.text: Made stern order relating to people in business

definitions.text: people in business

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A strict decree was issued concerning commercial folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made stern order' reads as issuing a strict command; 'order' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen are shopkeepers and skilled workers, people who earn a living through trade.

clue.text: Short of four babies?

definitions.text: Short of four babies?

parts.note: the abbreviated name for four babies born at one birth

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a family that is lacking four infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' looks like 'lacking' but means 'abbreviation for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadruplets are four siblings from one birth, commonly shortened in speech.

clue.text: So to speak, nearly all of our great dominions!

definitions.text: So to speak, nearly all of our great dominions!

parts.words: So to speak, nearly all of our great dominions
parts.note: the language spoken in almost all of Britain's former dominions such as Canada and Australia

explanation.surface: A patriotic boast about Britain's far-flung lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So to speak' looks like a filler phrase but literally points to speech. Dominions were self-governing countries of the British Empire, like Canada and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken across Canada, Australia and New Zealand is the language of England.

clue.text: He doesn't remain a wanderer

definitions.text: He doesn't remain a wanderer

parts.note: someone who never stays in one place is a roving traveller

explanation.surface: A man settles down and gives up roaming.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone giving up travel; read it as 'he doesn't remain, being a wanderer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a roving people moves from place to place, never staying put.

clue.text: Public Order Acts like these are against it

definitions.text: Public Order Acts like these are against it

parts.words: Public Order Acts like these are against it
parts.note: laws keeping public order exist to prevent violent disturbances of the peace

explanation.surface: Parliamentary legislation opposes some unnamed thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' reads as deeds, but the Public Order Acts are British laws against civil disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent public disturbances are exactly what public order legislation forbids.

clue.text: It had many centuries to establish itself as a world power

definitions.text: It had many centuries to establish itself as a world power

parts.words: It had many centuries to establish itself as a world power
parts.note: a century was a Roman army unit of about a hundred men, commanded by a centurion

explanation.surface: A great state took hundreds of years to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centuries' looks like spans of time but means Roman army units of a hundred soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's dominion over the Mediterranean world was built by its legions and their centuries.

clue.text: Manager sends players off even before such matches start

definitions.text: Manager sends players off even before such matches start

parts.words: Manager sends players off even before such matches start
parts.note: a team manager sends players away to travel to fixtures held at the opponents' ground

explanation.surface: A football boss dismisses his team before kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sends players off' suggests a referee's red card; here the players are dispatched to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixtures played on an opponent's ground require the team to travel there first.

clue.text: Smells cleaner

definitions.text: Smells cleaner

parts.note: read as an adjective plus a noun, a perfumed cleaning product

explanation.surface: Something gives off a fresher odour.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as verb plus comparative ('smells cleaner'), but is adjective plus noun: a cleaner that has been perfumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfumed washing bars are cleaners given a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Projected by a foe, it may appear on our screens!

definitions.text: Projected by a foe, it may appear on our screens!

parts.words: Projected by a foe, it may appear on our screens
parts.note: an enemy rocket launched at us shows up on radar screens

explanation.surface: A film shown by an enemy might be seen in our cinemas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projected' and 'screens' suggest cinema; they mean launched and radar displays.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket or projectile fired by an enemy is tracked as a blip on radar.

clue.text: Turned out Donald & Lewis expelled Aldo for fraud

definitions.text: fraud

indicators.note: letters turned out of their places are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: these four letters are removed from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Two men threw a third out of their company for cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled' removes the letters of ALDO from DONALD LEWIS, leaving DNLEWIS, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a deception practised to cheat someone out of money, a fraud.

clue.text: Closes up the gap in between

definitions.text: Closes up the gap in between

parts.words: Closes up the gap in between
parts.note: to close the distance between oneself and something is to approach it

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a space between two things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closes' looks like shuts, but means comes closer.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching something, coming closer to it, narrows the gap.

clue.text: It doesn't stop troops trying to impress the inspecting officer

definitions.text: It doesn't stop troops trying to impress the inspecting officer

parts.words: It doesn't stop troops trying to impress the inspecting officer
parts.note: a parade in which soldiers keep moving past a saluting officer

explanation.surface: Nothing prevents soldiers from showing off to a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It doesn't stop' reads as 'it doesn't prevent' but means the troops never halt as they file by.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade where soldiers file by a reviewing officer without halting.

clue.text: Like another to see if it did

definitions.text: Like another to see if it did

parts.words: Like another to see if it did
parts.note: looking like another thing, and also, split, put together again to see whether it worked

explanation.surface: Someone compares two things to check a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SEMBLED, it suggests reassembling something, while the whole word means looked like.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked like something else is to have been similar to it.

clue.text: They ought to be working away!.

definitions.text: They ought to be working away!.

parts.words: They ought to be working away
parts.note: people who should be at work but are not present

explanation.surface: An exhortation that people should be toiling hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working away' sounds like diligent toil; split it: they ought to be working, but are away.
explanation.definitionFit: People missing from work or school when they should be there.

clue.text: Labour's right to be upset by them!

definitions.text: Labour's right to be upset by them!

parts.words: Labour's right to be upset by them
parts.note: aggressive left-wing activists troubling the moderate wing of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: The Labour Party is justified in being annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour's right' reads as 'Labour is right'; it is Labour's right wing, unsettled by hard-left activists. Labour is a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive political activists, especially on the far left, unsettle moderates.

clue.text: The base of a great man's court!

definitions.text: The base of a great man's court!

parts.words: The base of a great man's court
parts.note: base as in low and servile, describing flatterers around a powerful person

explanation.surface: Refers to the foundation of a nobleman's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a foundation but means low-minded people: the fawning hangers-on of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants and flatterers are servile people fawning on the powerful.

clue.text: Looked like a burglar before he went to work

definitions.text: Looked like a burglar before he went to work

parts.words: Looked like a burglar before he went to work
parts.note: inspected a property in advance, as a thief does before a break-in

explanation.surface: Someone resembled a housebreaker on his way to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked like' reads as 'resembled' but means 'looked over in the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for reconnoitring a premises before robbing it.

clue.text: Enters something at numismatic display to get about 1000 points

definitions.text: Enters

indicators.note: the coin goes about, around, the added letters

parts.note: a numismatic display is a show of coins
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
E and S are the compass points east and south

explanation.surface: Someone submits an entry at a coin show hoping to win a high score.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a coin-show entrant chasing a score; 'about' is the container signal, with 'to get' merely linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To come in means to enter a place.

clue.text: Doesn't take a second cup of this coffee

definitions.text: Doesn't take a second cup of this coffee

parts.words: Doesn't take a second cup of this coffee
parts.note: a coffee made in no time at all, from powder and hot water

explanation.surface: A drinker refuses a refill of this brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't take a second cup' suggests declining more; it means the cup takes no more than a second to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Soluble coffee powder is ready immediately, without brewing.

clue.text: Birds

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as just 'Birds' with no count, for STOOD: cut short or swapped, and no source gives the rest

clue.text: Ingrained dirt

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as just 'Ingrained dirt' with no count, for TENSE: garbled or belongs to another entry, no source gives the rest

clue.text: Kept bringing up past recollections

definitions.text: Kept bringing up past recollections

parts.note: a keepsake that brings back memories of the past

explanation.surface: Someone kept harking back to old memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept' looks like a verb of repetition but describes a thing kept as a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir or keepsake retained to remind its owner of past events.

clue.text: I'm alone to torture these characters, feelings running high

definitions.text: feelings running high

indicators.note: torturing twists something out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lonely person, in a state of high passion, wants to torment others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these characters' tells you the letters of I'M ALONE TO are the ones rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred up, with passions high, is the state of being overcome by feeling.

clue.text: Very inclined to get soaking wet

definitions.text: Very inclined
definitions.meaning: sharply sloping, like a hill rising at a sharp angle

definitions.text: get soaking wet
definitions.meaning: to soak something in liquid, as tea leaves in hot water

explanation.surface: Someone keen to be drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharply sloping describes a hill; soaking in liquid describes tea brewing.

clue.text: Issue their description

definitions.text: Issue their description

parts.note: offspring are called issue, and the word for them describes how they come down from ancestors

explanation.surface: An order to publish someone's description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a verb meaning publish, but is a noun meaning offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring and their offspring in turn, the line coming down from an ancestor.
